problem: ALFRED task-completion agents predict navigation actions without identifying which object they are navigating toward, and ALFRED gives no object supervision for navigation steps. Transformer VLN agents also cannot handle ALFRED's roughly 50-step, multi-modal histories: beam search over completed paths is impossible with irreversible actions such as slicing, recurrent VLN-BERT only fits 4-6 step trajectories because of memory, and ET-style history encoders are shallow and not pretrained.
motivation: Instructional language is object-centric: 'head to the sink', 'pick up the potato on the counter'. Object-landmark prediction already helps navigation-only benchmarks (REVERIE, ObjectNav, VLN), so the authors expect navigation object targets to help joint navigation and manipulation too. They also want to use a full pretrained BERT/OSCAR stack, which requires separating per-step multimodal encoding from long-horizon temporal reasoning.
key_idea: Encode language and panoramic object detections independently at each timestep with a pretrained OSCAR/BERT transformer. Decode actions with a TransformerXL-style segment-recurrent decoder that cross-attends over cached past states. Supervise every navigation step with an object-centric navigation target (the goal object's bounding box, plus its parent receptacle) derived from ALFRED's planner subgoals.
insight: Object-centric navigation supervision is the component that matters most. With 18 side-view boxes, removing the navigation-object loss drops validation seen Task SR from 37.44 to 23.66 and unseen Task SR from 5.73 to 2.31. Long decoder memory also matters: with memory 1 instead of 200, seen SR falls from 36.22 to 21.95 and unseen from 4.39 to 1.58. OSCAR initialization beats plain BERT (36.22 vs 26.46 seen) and panoramic side views beat front-only (36.22 vs 25.31 seen). Parent-receptacle and visual-region-classification losses hurt the large 18-box model (all losses together: 28.54 seen SR) but help the smaller 9-box model on unseen, which the authors read as over-parameterization given ALFRED's limited data.
method: Panoramic object observations: after each navigation action the agent turns in place to collect left, back and right frames. A frozen Mask R-CNN (fine-tuned on AI2-THOR, from MOCA) gives 36 front and 18 per-side detections. Each detection embeds ResNet features, box coordinates, relative area and heading relative to the agent, then an MLP maps it into OSCAR's visual space.

Timestep-independent multimodal encoder: OSCAR-initialized BERT takes [CLS] goal [SEP] current step instruction [SEP] plus object embeddings. The state h_t is the element-wise product of the [CLS] hidden state and the last [SEP] hidden state.

Segment-Level Recurrent Action Decoder: a TransformerXL-style 2-layer, 8-head decoder with a 200-slot memory, trained on 10-step segments with gradients stopped across segments. It caches both encoder states and decoder states, and uses previous-action embeddings as queries that cross-attend to agent-state keys and values, producing time-dependent states.

Output heads: a 2-layer GeLU FFN predicts the action. Conditional scaling of token/object embeddings by the decoder state feeds a per-box classifier for the target object; IoU with the gold mask selects the target box during training. Manipulation targets come from the front view; navigation targets can come from any view.

Auxiliary losses: next-instruction prediction (binary, LWIT-style) to advance through step-by-step instructions; navigation object target L_NAV derived from the subgoal object visible at the end of each navigation segment; parent receptacle L_RECP; and visual region classification (15% of objects) L_VRC.

Action recovery at inference: after a failed navigation action, take the next most confident navigation action (as in MOCA). After a failed interaction, take the next most confident bounding box. Training uses teacher forcing, AdamW at lr 2e-5, and model selection by gold-trajectory action/object accuracy on val-seen.

setting.backbone: OSCAR-initialized BERT multimodal encoder (fine-tuned) + 2-layer TransformerXL-style action decoder (trained from scratch); frozen Mask R-CNN detector from MOCA
setting.training_data: ALFRED training expert demonstrations only, with no extra language or visual augmentation. Demonstrations are augmented with panoramic side-view frames and derived navigation-object and parent-receptacle labels. Encoder starts from OSCAR pretrained weights.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB; front view plus left/back/right views gathered by turning in place after navigation actions, represented as Mask R-CNN object detections; goal and step-by-step instructions
setting.action_space: ALFRED discrete low-level actions (5 navigation, e.g. MoveAhead/Turn/Look Up/Down; 7 manipulation, e.g. Pickup/ToggleOn/Slice) with the object mask chosen by selecting a detected bounding box
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT masks and planner subgoals used only to build training labels)

numbers_note: Metrics are ALFRED Task success (SR) and Goal-Condition success (GC), with path-length-weighted versions printed in parentheses (PLW-SR, PLW-GC). The ALFRED test-seen fold is recorded under split 'test' because 'test-seen' is not an allowed label. The paper does not say which validation configuration was submitted to the leaderboard. The validation ablation table is repeated in the appendix with one extra row (OSCAR/9/200/Nav O + VRC: seen 29.02 (21.40) / 36.27 (28.37), unseen 2.68 (1.42) / 11.04 (6.33)). Other ablation rows (9 side boxes, 0 side boxes, memory 1) are in the same table but not listed here.
results: On the ALFRED leaderboard EmBERT reaches 31.77 Task SR / 39.27 GC on test seen, beating LWIT (30.92), HLSM, MOCA, HiTUT and Seq2Seq but trailing ET (38.42) and ABP (44.55). On test unseen it reaches only 7.52 SR / 16.33 GC, beating MOCA (5.30) and Seq2Seq but trailing HLSM (16.29), ABP, HiTUT, LWIT and ET. The best validation configuration gets 37.44 / 5.73 Task SR on val seen / unseen versus MOCA's 18.90 / 3.65. Adding navigation object targets is the largest single gain (val seen SR 23.66 to 37.44).
limitations: Weak generalization to unseen rooms: only 7.52% test-unseen Task SR, below most competitive methods; no mapping or exploration.

Parent-receptacle and visual-region-classification auxiliary losses hurt the full 18-box model; the authors suspect over-parameterization for ALFRED's data size. No error bars or multiple seeds are reported.
Evaluated only on ALFRED (simulation, English, abstract locomotion, no novel object classes). The claimed applicability to VLN and CVDN is untested.
